attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps all four parts, minus the profanity. He states a present condition, so observation is the right kind.

contract.note: Reading 'done' as Huang's departure and 'no longer the titan' as NVIDIA ceasing to back dependent companies is an ordinary reading. 'Bubble popped' is a metaphor and is not separately testable. Choosing Nov 16 as the day to check is the evaluator's choice.

evidence.note: NVIDIA's 8-K says Huang resigned effective Nov 11 and Kress became interim CEO. This supports the departure part only, not withdrawal of financing.

Reuters (Nov 16–17): the financing platform is expected to continue, partners are still discussing deals, and a source saw no sign of a pause. This weighs against withdrawal, but anonymous reports of talks don't settle whether backing was available.

reviews.rationale: Huang's departure is documented, so the 'done' part holds. The financing part is not settled. No records show NVIDIA withdrawing backing. Reuters reports continuing talks and no pause, which leans against the claim, but it rests on anonymous sources and on discussions rather than binding commitments. The packet does not settle whether backing was available on Nov 16.

attribution.note: Zitron is rejecting someone else's view and states his own assertion about where the demand came from.

semantics.note: The core claim is causal: the demand was entirely caused by Huang's deals and NVIDIA's balance sheet. 'Entirely' is kept. 'Childish' is opinion. Treating 'if NVIDIA falters' as framing for the rejected view, not his own forecast, is correct.

contract.note: Testing whether relevant demand had any independent origin is fair to 'entirely'. Which demand counts ('said demand') is flagged as ambiguous, and the Q3 2026 period is the evaluator's choice.

evidence.note: Broadcom reports strong demand for its custom accelerators. Its fiscal quarter ended Aug 2, so it only partly overlaps the target period, and it does not trace how customers' purchases were funded.
Alphabet says TPU sales contributed to Q3 growth. That shows a rival supply channel, not that the demand behind it was independent of NVIDIA's dealmaking.

reviews.rationale: Both items show demand for rival accelerators, but neither traces customers' funding or shows that NVIDIA-linked demand had an independent origin. Under the contract, rival sales alone don't settle where the demand came from. The packet neither establishes nor refutes the 'entirely' claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own unqualified assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: Both 'vast majority' quantifiers are kept, and the two populations stay separate. It is a firm present-tense claim, so observation is right.

contract.note: The plain reading (an overwhelming majority, willingness at stated prices, affordability from sustainable funds) is ordinary. The global scope and the Q3 2026 period are the evaluator's choices.

evidence.note: US conjoint survey of 314 people (March 2026): 63% chose a paid plan at least some of the time. The choices were hypothetical, the sample is US-only, and fieldwork predates the target quarter. It covers only clause one.
Card data: 2.9% of US consumers paid a major AI provider in April 2026. That measures actual payment, not willingness or compute affordability, and it predates the target quarter.

reviews.rationale: Neither item measures worldwide willingness to pay in Q3 2026, and nothing measures how many paying compute customers cannot afford their purchases. The survey leans against clause one but is earlier, US-only and hypothetical. Low actual payment does not show unwillingness. Neither clause is settled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own narrative assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: Both factual parts are captured, but 'entire' is dropped from 'entire stock market'. The contract restores it. The 'attack you viciously' part is reasonably left out.

contract.note: Profit as 'making money', US indexes, and the inferred 2023–24 period are ordinary readings. The contract's line that an unknown accounting basis rules out any verdict is an extra rule that the speaker did not supply. The outcome here does not depend on it.

evidence.note: Morningstar: Nvidia accounted for 19% of 2024 market gains and AI demand drove growth stocks, but it says gains were 'not all about AI'. This partly bears on the market clause, but not on the whole market or on profits.

Secondhand Sept 2023 report that Midjourney was 'reportedly profitable'. It weighs against the 'only semiconductor companies' clause, but it gives no accounts or comparable basis and the original source was not read.

reviews.rationale: The market evidence shows AI-linked concentration in 2024, not that the entire market depended on AI. The only counterexample on profits is an unverified secondhand report with no comparable profit basis, as the contract requires. Neither clause is settled on this packet.
